name: Interdigitating Dendritic Cell Sarcoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunophenotypic Diagnostic Criteria for IDCS

criteria.description: Presence of spindle to ovoid tumor cells with interdigitating cytoplasmic processes on histology
Tumor cells positive for S100 protein and vimentin, negative for CD1a and CD21
Exclusion of other dendritic cell neoplasms and histiocytic sarcoma by immunohistochemistry
Presentation as a localized or disseminated mass, often involving lymph nodes or extranodal sites

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with characteristic morphology plus immunophenotypic profile (S100+, CD1a-, CD21-) and exclusion of other dendritic/histiocytic neoplasms
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires expert hematopathological evaluation and immunohistochemical staining panel.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically localized or generalized lymph node enlargement
Commonly involves skin, spleen, or soft tissue

common.symptomName: Constitutional B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
common.notes: May be present in disseminated disease

occasional.notes: Liver enlargement in some disseminated cases

occasional.symptomName: Bone pain due to marrow involvement
searchTerms: aching bones due to marrow disease

occasional.notes: Cough or dyspnea if lung involved
searchTerms: respiratory symptoms due to lung involvement

occasional.notes: Very rare central nervous system infiltration
searchTerms: neurological deficits from brain or spinal involvement
nerve problems due to CNS disease
weakness or sensory loss from CNS

rare.notes: Rare orbital masses causing visual symptoms
searchTerms: vision issues due to eye socket involvement

laboratory: Mild anemia or cytopenias in disseminated disease
Negative for lineage-specific markers of lymphoma or carcinoma
imaging: CT or PET-CT showing lymphadenopathy and extranodal masses
MRI for CNS or soft tissue involvement
genetic: No recurrent genetic abnormalities identified; diagnosis based on morphology and immunophenotype
other: Immunohistochemistry positive for S100, vimentin, fascin
Negative for CD1a, CD21, CD35, and other dendritic cell markers

distinguishingFeatures: Different histological pattern with follicular dendritic cell markers
Strong positivity for melanocytic markers (HMB-45, Melan-A)

redFlags: Presence of extranodal masses with systemic symptoms
Failure to respond to conventional lymphoma therapies
references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
Chan JK, Fletcher CD, Nayler SJ, Cooper K. Interdigitating dendritic cell sarcoma: a clinicopathologic analysis of four cases. Am J Surg Pathol. 1995.
